reports.title: 2026 ApprovalPrep Document Readiness Index: A Catalog of 100 Public Application Checklists
reports.summary: A transparent 100-source catalog across rental, employment/income verification, mortgage/home-loan, and small-business funding preparation, with primary-source coding and explicit limitations.
reports.methodology: The release catalogs 100 public sources in a balanced four-category sampling frame. URL/source metadata is coded for all 100; item-level preparation signals are reported only for eight primary sources marked as deep reviewed. It is not a market survey, approval model, or claim that every source requires the same documents.

sections.heading: 100 public sources, four categories
sections.body: The catalog contains 25 sources each for rental applications, employment and income verification, mortgage and home-loan preparation, and small-business funding.

sections.heading: A split-format information problem
sections.body: The catalog contains 82 HTML sources and 18 PDF sources, showing why applicants often need a clean source list and copy trail.

sections.heading: Authority is distributed
sections.body: The catalog includes 21 government or public-authority sources alongside financial institutions, universities, housing organizations, and private operators.

sections.heading: Primary-source preparation pattern
sections.body: Eight primary sources were deep reviewed. Those sources repeatedly emphasized factual identity, income or employment, assets or fund sources, and traceable support. This pattern is not applied to sources that were only cataloged.

sections.heading: What the report does not claim
sections.body: The dataset does not measure approval odds, rankings, traffic, market share, or applicant outcomes. The requester’s current instructions remain authoritative.

reports.title: Apartment Application Prep Report
reports.summary: A public report on the paperwork areas renters should organize before applying for an apartment.
reports.methodology: This report is based on ApprovalPrep rental pages, template previews, and public self-service checklist rules. It is educational and does not claim housing approval outcomes.

sections.heading: Core readiness areas
sections.body: Rental preparation usually starts with identity details, income proof, rental history, explanation letters when needed, and a clear copy trail.

sections.heading: Common packet gaps
sections.body: Applicants often need cleaner dates, consistent address history, income-source clarity, and a short explanation that matches the supporting documents.

sections.heading: Boundary
sections.body: ApprovalPrep helps organize truthful self-service paperwork. It does not contact landlords, screen applicants, create fake documents, or guarantee acceptance.

reports.title: Small Business Funding Document Prep Report
reports.summary: A public report explaining the document-prep areas small businesses can organize before funding conversations.
reports.methodology: This report uses ApprovalPrep business-funding pages and checklist rules. It is not lending advice, underwriting advice, or a financing guarantee.

sections.heading: Document categories
sections.body: Business funding prep often includes ownership facts, revenue proof, tax documents, bank statements, use-of-funds notes, and business context.

sections.heading: Preparation principle
sections.body: A stronger packet separates evidence from explanation and makes the reviewer’s document request easier to follow.

sections.heading: Boundary
sections.body: ApprovalPrep does not submit applications, negotiate terms, create financial records, or promise funding.
